source.title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes

accepted.question_text: Which finite simple groups occur as automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes, where a chiral d-polytope is an abstract rank-d polytope whose automorphism group has exactly two flag-orbits and adjacent flags lie in different orbits?

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Determine which finite simple groups are automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Which sporadic finite simple groups occur as automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes?

evidence.quote: Problem 2 Determine which sporadic finite simple groups are automorphism groups of chiral d-polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a chiral polytope whose monodromy group on flags, generated by the involutions r_i that send a flag to its i-adjacent flag, is not a string C-group?

evidence.quote: Problem 3 Is there a chiral polytope whose monodromy group is not a string C-group?

accepted.question_text: Does every chiral polytope have a minimal regular cover, meaning a regular polytope that admits a flag action onto it and is covered in this way by every other regular cover?

evidence.quote: Problem 4 Does every chiral polytope have a minimal regular cover?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of chiral covers of polytopes: define the right notion of quotient and cover in the chiral setting, and formulate the analogue of the regular-cover theory for chiral polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 5 Develop a theory of chiral covers of polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Characterize all pairs (K, P) consisting of a chiral polytope K and a regular polytope P for which the chirality group of the mix K♦P equals the chirality group of K itself.

evidence.quote: Problem 6 Can we characterize all pairs (K,P) consisting of a chiral polytope K and a regular polytope P such that X(K♦P) = X(K)?

accepted.question_text: Determine conditions under which the Petrie scheme of a chiral polytope is acoptic, meaning that each proper face is contained in at most one flag of the Petrie scheme.

evidence.quote: Problem 7 Determine conditions under which the Petrie scheme of a chiral polytope is acoptic.

accepted.question_text: Determine conditions under which the Petrie path of a chiral polytope is a polygon.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 Determine conditions under which the Petrie path of a chiral polytope is a polygon.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a chiral polytope whose left Petrie paths are polygons but whose right Petrie paths are not polygons?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 Is there a chiral polytope whose left Petrie paths are polygons, but whose right Petrie paths are not?

accepted.question_text: For each integer k ≥ 2, either find a chiral 4k-polytope whose right Petrie paths and left Petrie paths have different lengths, or prove that no such chiral 4k-polytope exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 10 Find examples of chiral 4k-polytopes (where k ≥ 2) with the property that the length of the right Petrie paths does not coincide with the length of the left Petrie paths, or prove their non-existence.

accepted.question_text: Determine the pairs of positive integers (m, n) for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope whose right Petrie paths have length m and whose left Petrie paths have length n.

evidence.quote: Problem 11 Determine the pairs (m, n) for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope with right Petrie paths of length m and left Petrie paths of length n.

accepted.question_text: Determine the integers n for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope whose right and left Petrie paths both have length n.

evidence.quote: Problem 12 Determine the integers n for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope with right and left Petrie paths of length n.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist chiral tessellations of spherical space-forms?

evidence.quote: Problem 13 Determine whether there exist chiral tessellations of spherical space-forms.

accepted.question_text: Examine locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type.

evidence.quote: Problem 14 Examine locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type.

accepted.question_text: Determine all pairs of spherical or toroidal (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2 such that at least one of K1 or K2 is chiral and there exists a chiral d-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to K1 and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K2.

evidence.quote: Problem 15 Determine all spherical or toroidal (d − 1)-polytopes K1 and K2 such that at least one of K1 or K2 is chiral and there exists a chiral d-polytope with facets isomorphic to K1 and vertex-figures isomorphic to K2.

accepted.question_text: Determine all finite universal locally toroidal polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 16 Determine all finite universal locally toroidal polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Determine all pairs of spherical (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2 for which there exists a chiral d-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to K1 and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K2.

evidence.quote: Problem 17 Determine all spherical (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2 for which there exists a chiral d-polytope with facets isomorphic to K1 and vertex-figures isomorphic to K2.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the chiral maps that fail to be polyhedra, that is, the chiral maps that do not satisfy the abstract-polytope conditions needed to be rank-3 polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 18 Characterize chiral maps which are not polyhedra.

accepted.question_text: Determine all positive integers g for which there exist chiral maps, equivalently chiral polyhedra, on orientable surfaces of genus g.

evidence.quote: Problem 19 Determine all positive integers g for which there are chiral maps (polyhedra) on orientable surfaces with genus g.

accepted.question_text: Let nr(g) be the number of regular polytopes on orientable surfaces of genus at most g and let nch(g) be the number of chiral polytopes on such surfaces. Determine the limit of nr(g)/nch(g) as g → ∞, if this limit exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 20 Let nr(g) and nch(g) denote respectively the number of regular and chiral polytopes on orientable surfaces of genus at most g. Determine limg→∞ nr(g)/nch(g) if the limit exists.

accepted.question_text: Determine all pairs {p, q}, with p and q in {3, 4, ...} ∪ {∞}, for which there exist infinite chiral maps, equivalently infinite chiral polyhedra, of Schläfli type {p, q}.

evidence.quote: Problem 21 Determine all pairs {p, q} with p, q ∈ {3, 4, . . . } ∪ {∞} for which there exist infinite chiral maps (polyhedra) with Schlafli type {p, q}.

accepted.question_text: Determine which noncompact surfaces without boundary admit embeddings of chiral maps.

evidence.quote: Problem 22 Determine which noncompact surfaces without boundary admit embeddings of chiral maps.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there are infinite families of chiral quotients of every regular honeycomb in hyperbolic 3-space, 4-space, and 5-space.

evidence.quote: Problem 23 Determine the existence of infinite families of chiral quotients of all regular honeycombs in hyperbolic 3-, 4- and 5-space.

accepted.question_text: For every regular polytope K, does there exist a chiral extension of K that covers every other extension of K?
accepted.context_brief: universal chiral extensions of regular polytopes

evidence.quote: Problem 24 Determine whether for every (any) regular polytope K there exists a chiral extension which covers every extension of K.

accepted.question_text: Does every chiral polytope K with regular facets admit a chiral extension whose Schläfli symbol has any prescribed last entry?

evidence.quote: Problem 25 Does every chiral polytope K with regular facets admit a chiral extension with prescribed last entry of the Schlafli symbol?

accepted.question_text: Does every finite chiral polytope K with regular facets admit a finite chiral extension whose Schläfli symbol has any prescribed last entry?

evidence.quote: Problem 26 Does every chiral finite polytope K with regular facets admit a finite chiral extension with prescribed last entry of the Schlafli symbol?

accepted.question_text: Does every orientably regular d-polytope, for d ≥ 2, admit a chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 27 Does every orientably regular d-polytope admit a chiral extension (d ≥ 2)?

accepted.question_text: Does every finite orientably regular d-polytope, for d ≥ 2, admit a finite chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 28 Does every orientably regular finite d-polytope admit a finite chiral extension (d ≥ 2)?

accepted.question_text: Does every orientably regular polytope admit an infinite chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 29 Does every orientably regular polytope admit an infinite chiral extension?

accepted.question_text: Does every convex regular polytope admit a chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 30 Does every convex regular polytope admit a chiral extensions?

accepted.question_text: Given regular or chiral (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2, does there exist a chiral d-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to K1 and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K2?

evidence.quote: Problem 31 Given regular (or chiral) (d − 1)-polytopes K1 and K2, does there exist a chiral d-polytope P with faces isomorphic to K1 and vertex-figures isomorphic to K2?

accepted.question_text: For regular or enantiomorphic forms of chiral polytopes K1 and K2, not both regular, determine the automorphism group of the universal chiral amalgamation {K1, K2}_ch and give conditions under which this universal amalgamation is finite.

evidence.quote: Problem 32 Determine the group of the universal amalgamation {K1, K2}ch and give conditions under which this is finite, where K1 and K2 are regular or enantiomorphic forms of chiral polytopes, not both regular.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a flat chiral or regular d-polytope for every d ≥ 3, where flat means that every facet contains every vertex?

evidence.quote: Problem 33 Does there exist a flat d-polytopes for every d ≥ 3?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a (k, m)-flat d-polytope for each triple (k, m, d) with 0 < k + 1 < m ≤ d − 1, where (k, m)-flat means that every m-face contains every k-face?

evidence.quote: Problem 34 Does there exist a (k, m)-flat d-polytopes for each triple (k, m, d) with 0 < k + 1 < m ≤ d − 1?

accepted.question_text: Determine the function m^ch_d giving, for each rank d, the minimum possible number of flags of a chiral d-polytope.

evidence.quote: Problem 35 Find the value of mchd as a function of d.

accepted.question_text: Develop the realization theory for chiral polytopes: describe and organize their realizations in geometric spaces in a way analogous to the established realization theory for regular polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 36 Develop the details of the realization theory for chiral polytopes.

accepted.question_text: Classify all finite and infinite chiral k-polytopes in R^d, in the range k < d for finite polytopes and k ≤ d for infinite polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 37 Classify all finite and infinite chiral k-polytopes in Rd (where k < d for finite polytopes, and k ≤ d for infinite ones).

accepted.question_text: Classify all finite chiral polyhedra in Euclidean 4-space E^4.

evidence.quote: Problem 38 Classify all finite chiral polyhedra in E4.

accepted.question_text: Classify all infinite chiral 4-polytopes in Euclidean 4-space E^4.

evidence.quote: Problem 39 Classify all infinite chiral 4-polytopes in E4.

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF structure. Open problems appear explicitly as Problems 1-39 across Sections 3-8 on pages 6-19.

Extracted all explicitly numbered problem statements from Sections 3-8: Problems 1-6 (group structures), 7-12 (Petrie paths), 13-17 (topological considerations), 18-22 (rank 3), 23-35 (higher ranks), and 36-39 (realizations).
Rewrote each numbered problem into standalone wording while preserving the source problem statement and only adding brief in-source terminology expansions where needed.
No duplicates were merged. The paper presents 39 distinct numbered open problems and each was kept as its own item.
Accepted all 39 numbered problems because each has an explicit problem label and a verbatim supporting quote with a page number from the PDF.
